HorizonCache — Consolidation (E56)

Causal safe-horizon prediction for flow-model acceleration · FLUX.1-dev 512px/28 · N=100 paired samples · commit fc37f45 · cluster H100 (Run:AI)

1 · Executive summary

Verdict: STRONG KEEP for adaptive_1.25 (the conservative headroom-adaptive stride).

Headline. FLUX N=100: adaptive_1.25 @ 2.51× = +2.20 dB vs matched SeaCache (95% CI [+1.79, +2.62], win 85%).

Bounded claim. A conservative headroom-adaptive stride extension shifts the FLUX SeaCache frontier upward in the ~1.7–2.7× achieved-speedup band, while aggressive jumps still overshoot.

Family finding (N=100, honest nuance). The scale-up sees the whole adaptive family: jf_max = 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 all clear the strong-KEEP rule in-band (every in-band CI excludes 0). This is because the stride is headroom-capped — jf_max is a soft ceiling the gate rarely reaches when the cache is fresh — so a larger cap mostly does not change in-band behaviour. adaptive_1.25 stays the recommended conservative operating point (safest cap, best in the mid band, ties 1.5); it beats the fixed regrid_1.25 at matched speed. The robust thing is the mechanism, not one magic cap.

What failed. The overshoot is a high-τ / high-speed effect common to every cap (τ0.65 ≈ 3.4×: −0.14 to −0.16 dB, CI excludes 0 on the negative side) — a measured loss, not a caveat. Note this is the headroom-capped adaptive_2.0; the uncapped discrete jump_2.0 action (no headroom gate) was KILLed earlier and is not the same thing. SD3 replication is unavailable (no MMDiT generation harness in the module). Learned v1 remains PARK.

2 · Background (from the deck)

  • SeaCache signal. One cheap score off the modulated input h (before the L-block stack, Wiener-filtered relative-L1) → refresh vs cache.
  • h-drift / headroom. Accumulate the drift; headroom =1−acc/τ measures how far the current computation stays trustworthy.
  • cache vs jump. Cache freezes the block residual but keeps the σ-grid (saves the block stack inside a node); a jump takes a longer σ-stride that removes a whole node.
  • Original FLUX tie expectation. E53 found SeaCache's rel-L1 ranks the oracle safe-jump length only weakly (Spearman −0.50) → a naïve jump gate was expected to tie.
  • E56 update. FLUX has a conservative safe-stride pocket: refresh often (low τ) yet still save compute with small headroom-gated jumps — a gentler quality/speed tradeoff exactly where SeaCache's frontier drops steepest.

3 · Method

HorizonCache adaptive headroom stride. In cache territory (acc<τ) the stride factor is jf = 1 + (jf_max−1)·headroom, headroom = 1−acc/τ — small safe strides when the cache is fresh, larger (capped at jf_max) when there is headroom.

Scheduler. regrid: off-grid target σ_target=σ_i+jf·(σ_{i+1}−σ_i), then re-space the remaining tail to 0 (net −1 node). Every jump logged. Jumps disabled ⇒ SeaCache exactly (fair by identity).

Compute accounting (achieved, not nominal). fresh=1 forward, cache/jump≈1/L (L=57); jumps additionally remove executed nodes. We report block-stack-equivalent and measured wall speedup.

Fair comparison. ΔPSNR at matched achieved speedup — the SeaCache PSNR(speedup) curve interpolated at each HorizonCache image's own speedup, paired per prompt×seed, percentile bootstrap 95% CI. Same protocol as the sig run; not changed here.

4 · Experiments

  • FLUX scale-up. N=100 paired samples (50 prompts × 2 seeds), 512px/28 Euler, bf16+bnb4, τ∈[0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.65].
  • Methods. full · uniform · TeaCache · SeaCache · regrid_1.25 · adaptive_1.25/1.5/2.0.
  • SD3. unavailable path — the module's generation harness hooks FLUX transformer internals (load_flux_pipeline/sample_flux); there is no MMDiT/SD3 harness. Running SD3 needs a new h-signal hook + Euler loop for SD3.5-medium, not just a weight download. Documented, not stalled.
  • Stats. per-image paired matched-speedup deltas; 5000-sample percentile bootstrap for mean ΔPSNR, mean ΔLPIPS and win-rate.

At the headline point (2.51×), matched ΔLPIPS = +0.029 (95% CI [+0.02, +0.04]).

Qualitative (full · SeaCache@matched · adaptive→1.25@matched · aggressive · error). Honest read: at near-matched quality (~35+ dB) the gain is sub-visible — mostly metric/frontier-level; it becomes visually obvious only where SeaCache's stale cache breaks down (low-PSNR prompts). The value is a frontier shift, not a per-image night-and-day change.

6 · Mechanism — why adaptive_1.25 survives

The one figure: SeaCache vs HorizonCache at matched speed. Same fresh count, same speed — HorizonCache removes whole nodes with small safe jumps and finishes earlier.
σ-schedule semantics: cache keeps the grid; regrid/adaptive remove a node.
Where the steps go at matched speed — cache saves the block stack inside a node; a jump saves the whole node.
Staleness ↔ stride: larger jumps only when headroom is high, capped at jf_max.

7 · Failures

Aggressive-jump overshoot: large strides remove nodes where the field still curves; integration error compounds to the end.
  • High-τ / 3×+ band (all caps). At τ0.65 (≈3.4×) every adaptive cap turns to a significant loss vs matched SeaCache (−0.14 to −0.16 dB, CI excludes 0, win ≤24%) — pushing the refresh threshold high and jumping removes nodes where the field still curves; error compounds to the end (the deck's DP-surrogate lesson, made visible).
  • Uncapped discrete jump_2.0. The unconditional jf=2.0 action (no headroom gate) remains KILL — distinct from the headroom-capped adaptive_2.0, which is safe in-band.
  • v1 supervision. Full-rollout frontier-improvement labels give a real positive class (~70% jump-helpful) but the learned binary policy ties the heuristic on the small dataset — a useful negative; needs a much larger label set.
  • SD3/FLUX mismatch. Not testable here — no SD3 harness; the wider-band hypothesis (SD3 jf_max≈1.5–2.0) stays open.
